acceptance: A project.planning.requested event with project=scout-knowledge-lib does NOT trigger may-agent-project-planner.
A project.planning.requested event with project=may-agent still triggers may-agent-project-planner.
Non-project-scoped event types (e.g. metric.breach with metricIds) continue to match correctly.
Existing tests pass and a new test covers the cross-project filter.
forbidden: Do not break event-type-only handlers that intentionally receive all events of a type.
Do not change app event router behavior (shouldOfferToApp already works correctly).

verification.reason: Added eventProjectId helper and project-scope filter in triggerSubscribers. 3 new tests pass (cross-project mismatch blocked, same-project fires, no-project-field fires). All 7 cron tests pass, 24 related tests pass, TypeScript check clean.

context.root_cause: Cron buildEventSubscriptions indexes handlers by event type only. triggerSubscribers fires all handlers subscribed to project.planning.requested regardless of the event's project field. The app event router (shouldOfferToApp/matchesSelector in project-app-loader.ts) already filters correctly, but cron's workflow handler dispatch bypasses this — the event arrives on the bus, cron's subscribeToBus catches it, and triggerSubscribers fires without project filtering.
context.evidence: handler.started event for may-agent-project-planner at timestamp 1781367454489, triggered by scout-knowledge-lib's scheduled-library-maintenance event at 1781367454488.
context.fix_direction: Either (a) add a projectId field to CronEntry and filter in triggerSubscribers, or (b) make installWorkflowHandlers store the project app's event selectors alongside the subscription and check them before firing.
